0: He whose nature is un-setting light, [who is the essence] of both luminous things and dark things,
1: who alone is within, and within whom are both luminous things and dark things —
2: He alone is the essential nature of all beings, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>);
3: for the totality of existing things is indeed His power (<s>śakti</s>), which is of the nature of sovereignty.
4: And <s>śakti</s> (power) does not desire any separation from the nature of the possessor of <s>śakti</s>;
5: the identity of these two is eternal, like that of fire and its capacity to burn.
6: He alone is the divine <s>Bhairava</s>, characterized by the sustaining of the universe,
7: for the entirety [of creation] is reflected by His <s>śakti</s> in the mirror of His own Self.
8: This is His supreme Goddess (<s>Devī</s>), ever-eager to reflect upon her own essential nature;
9: whose fullness in all states of existence is neither less nor more.
10: This God (<s>Deva</s>), with this Goddess (<s>Devī</s>), always eager for the delight of play (<s>krīḍā</s>),
11: the all-pervading Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>) simultaneously brings about the manifold creations and dissolutions.
12: That which is His supreme capacity to accomplish the utterly impossible —
13: that itself is His absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), and the nature of consciousness (<s>bodharūpatā</s>).
14: Limited luminosity is indeed the characteristic of the insentient (<s>jaḍa</s>);
15: consciousness (<s>bodha</s>) is different from the insentient, since it is not limited.
16: Thus, for this autonomous One, differentiated by His own powers (<s>śakti</s>),
17: the creations and dissolutions, [being] within His own Self, abide as His very nature.
18: The extreme variety among them — what is above, below, and across,
19: the worlds and their parts, and the consciousness of pleasure and pain —
20: the non-recognition (<s>aparijñāna</s>) of this [Self] has been described as His own free will (<s>svātantrya</s>);
21: that indeed is <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of worldly existence), which is terrifying for the deluded.
22: Through the grace (<s>prasāda</s>) of that very [Lord], or from the <s>guru</s> (teacher) and tradition (<s>āgama</s>),
23: or from the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) of the Supreme Lord — from whatever source it may come,
24: the recognition (<s>parijñāna</s>) of that reality — that is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) from the Supreme Lord;
25: that fullness of the awakened ones is also known as <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living).
26: These two — bondage and liberation — from the standpoint of the essential nature of the Supreme Lord,
27: are not different, for in reality there is no division in the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>).
28: Thus, <s>Bhairava</s>, abiding in the trident of the powers of will (<s>icchā</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>),
29: is investigated as the essential nature of all existing things.
30: In order to easily awaken students of tender intellect,
31: these fifteen verses have been uttered by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.
